items.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You would hear these people play in these sewers and I’d go in and see them, you know.

ctx.x: They were hollerin’ the blues and then there was Dan Grissom, he could really sing, you know. And then, Muddy Waters, and let’s see, Memphis Slim. You would hear these people play in these sewers and I’d go in and see them, you know. They say, “What would you like?” I’d say, “Some champagne” and they would buy me champagne and I’d listen to them.
Let’s stick on Memphis Slim for a second. Was his music considered in the community to be less sophisticated than some of the other piano players?
I guess so because people didn’t understand it as well as they… he made most of his money in Europe, though.
